The premises are that most animals have fur and are good pets, that cats have no fur, and that dogs are not commonly seen as pets. "Most" is not "all," so it does not assign fur or pet status to any specific animal. The premises never state that dogs are furry or that cats are pets. A countermodel confirms this: cats and dogs both lack fur and are not pets, and the premises still hold. Both conclusions fail there, so the conjunction is not entailed. The submitted "Yes" is wrong.
